title: Responder scratchpad: timeboxed mitigation guidelines for API degradations
content:
Purpose:
This is a responder-oriented scratchpad: quick, timeboxed guidance for the first 30/60/120 minutes when API anomalies present as timeouts, widespread 429s, degraded streaming, or rising 5xx/error rates.

Context / constraints:
- Lightweight, assume noisy telemetry in early minutes.
- Prioritize user-facing impact mitigation (latency & availability) over deep root cause analysis in T+0.
- Use these as a checklist to escalate or handoff to engineering teams.
- This is intentionally terse — meant for pager-first response.

Signals that should trigger use of this doc:
- Service error rate (5xx) > 1% for >5 min on main prod route OR
- Latency p50 or p95 spikes above SLO thresholds (example: p95 > 1200ms) OR
- Streaming sessions showing partial/garbled chunks / heartbeats dropped OR
- Burst of 429s correlated with throttler metrics or redis rate limiter counters.

Fast triage (first 0-10 minutes) — checklist (timebox: 10m):
1) Acknowledge incident in PagerDuty and add short summary. Start a temporary Slack channel (#ops-incident-<shortid>).
2) Gather quick impact scope: API endpoints affected, geo regions, client teams (use token prefix), error codes distribution.
   - Grafana: service:api->errors-by-code, latency-by-route, requests-per-second.
   - Quick queries (examples):
     - PromQL: sum(rate(http_server_exceptions_total[5m])) by (status)
     - PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
3) Check capacity/backends: GPU pool metrics, serving-runtime-rejects, queue lengths, and shard CPU.
4) If 429s are dominant, check rate-limiter dashboard and Redis/etcd counters.
5) If streams degrade: check websocket/proxy layer and keepalive counts (nginx/h2c/edge-proxy).
6) If timeouts: identify where timeouts originate (ingress timeout vs downstream).
   - Compare client-side timeout vs internal service timeouts in traces (jaeger/tempo).

Immediate mitigations (first 10-30 minutes) — apply what fits, timebox to 20m total:
A) Traffic shaping & routing
   - Enable fallback model variant / cheaper model (if configured) for non-premium tokens. Command: toggle rollout -> canary->fallback (console shortcut).
   - Route traffic to a different region / capacity pool if cross-region fallback exists.
   - Temporarily take non-critical routes out of rotation (e.g., batch ingestion endpoints).
B) Throttle & shed load
   - Increase global rate-limiter limits only if backed by capacity; otherwise tighten limits for unauthenticated or free-tier tokens.
   - Turn on aggressive prefix-caching for repeated requests if cache path present.
C) Scale & capacity adjustments
   - Trigger autoscale override for Dedicated pools (burst mode) or increase worker replicas for async queues.
   - If GPU queue backlog high, consider increasing worker batch size (short term) only if it reduces total backlog without violating latency SLOs.
D) Streaming-specific quick fixes
   - If proxies (edge) are dropping streaming chunks, rollback recent proxy config (nginx/h2) change.
   - If keepalive/idle timeouts misconfigured, extend connection timeout on proxy to match runtime (short-term safety).
E) Fail open/close decisions
   - For persistent high latency, enable synchronous fallback to stubbed responses for certain feature flags. Document which flags changed.

Quick diagnostics & commands (use opportunistically):
- kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=api -o wide --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
- kubectl logs -n inference deployment/api -c server --since=10m | tail -n 200
- curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?model=redwood-1"  (check headers, timing)
- redis-cli -h redis-prod INFO | grep cmdstat_incr  (hot counters)
- Query tracing: tempo query -> filter by trace id in last 15m with high latency

Escalation criteria (when to pull in infra/serving/runtime/SDRT):
- Error rate > 3% for 30+ minutes despite traffic shaping
- Evidence of hardware degradation (GPU OOMs, NPU failures, NIC errors)
- Datastore (redis/pg) saturation correlated with request errors
- Streaming layer dropping connection heartbeats after config change

Short-term recovery play examples (choose 1-2, keep changes reversible):
1) 429 flood from misconfigured client: identify top tokens -> apply immediate token-level reject with clear reason -> notify client team -> re-enable after fix.
2) Backend model latency bump: switch to smaller model variant for affected route -> monitor p95 drop -> plan rollback window.
3) Edge proxy memory leak (recent deploy): rollback last proxy config -> drain connections -> observe stream stability.

Notes on observability & sanity checks post-mitigation (first 60-120 minutes):
- Validate p50/p95 and error rate falling toward baseline. Wait at least 2 aggregation windows (5m each) before declaring partial recovery.
- Check downstream effects: consumer backpressure, DLQ growth, and billing anomalies.
- Annotate the incident in Grafana when key mitigations were toggled (time-stamped).

Runbook fragments: specific handling by failure type
- Timeouts:
  * Confirm which hop is timing out (edge vs runtime vs model inference).
  * If runtime inference: check KV cache hit rate, batch sizes, and GPU queue depth.
  * If edge/ingress: check network flaps and proxy connection limits.
- 429s (rate limit):
  * Classify 429s by reason header (quota vs concurrency vs custom throttler).
  * If throttler misfiring: flip throttler to permissive mode for internal clients, isolate public traffic.
- Degraded streaming:
  * Look for partial chunk buffers; identify whether data path or real-time encoder is struggling.
  * Check chunk-size histogram and proxy downstream backlog.
- Elevated error rates (5xx):
  * Map error types (model OOM, runtime panic, validation errors).
  * For validation/config errors: revert recent config changes or feature flags.

Post-incident (post T+120) checklist — capture before handoff:
- Save relevant logs, trace ids, and exact mitigation commands.
- Create an incident ticket with timeline (T0, mitigations, metrics snapshots).
- Identify owners for root-cause investigation (runtime, infra, gateways, client).
- If rollback was used, schedule safe re-deployment window and test plan.
- Draft a short customer-facing note if SLA risk existed.

Open questions / TODOs (to resolve in follow-up):
- Can we add a single "panic button" in Console to trigger model-fallback + throttler-soften for affected tokens? (worth engineering spike)
- Build a pre-baked dashboard view that correlates rate-limiter counters, GPU queue, and streaming chunk errors in one panel.
- Create token-scoped quick-disable (UI + API) with audit log for emergency throttling.

Quick templates (copy into Slack or PD summary):
- Short ack: "Acked — investigating. Initial impact: <percent> requests failing, top error: <code>. Triage steps running: dashboards + capacity checks. Oncall: @<name>"
- Mitigation note: "Applied model-fallback to route /v1/generate for free-tier tokens at 14:22 UTC; p95 latency dropped from 1800ms -> 850ms within 10m. Continuing monitoring."

Notes-to-self style and signals log (examples to paste into incident):
- 14:06 see spike p95, traces show inference time jump from 300ms -> 1200ms.
- 14:12 toggled fallback -> partial recovery.
- 14:35 observed redis rate-limit counters spike -> suspect token replay.

References & links to existing artifacts:
- Rate limiter design doc (Confluence): /display/infra/ratelimiter-design
- Streaming proxy tuning notes: /display/infra/proxy-stream-tuning

Versioning / doc provenance:
- Author: Ethan Morales (eng-sre).
- This is a living draft; please annotate with improvements after next incident (tag: responder-scratchpad).

End of scratchpad.
